_comment: Commands are the suite's addressable entry points. This file is the single source of truth: scripts/generate_commands.py renders commands/<name>.md from it and verifies every declared section exists in the owning skill. Never edit a generated command file by hand; edit this manifest and re-run the generator. A command earns its place by the rule in docs/COMMANDS.md: the router, or a skill section that runs standalone with its own inputs and outputs. Skills themselves are not commands — they are already invocable by name.

commands.description: Route any task to the right rnov24 skill and flow. Use when starting work, when unsure which skill applies, or when a task spans phases.
commands.name: rnov
commands.output: Three-line classification plus the next skill to run.
steps: Classify the task: size, novelty, surface, risk (see `using-rnov-skills`).
Pick the standard flow for the task, or the earliest phase whose inputs exist.
Load only the chosen skill's SKILL.md; do not open five skills to be safe.
If no skill fits, say so and stop instead of forcing the nearest one.

commands.description: Run the full Goldfish protocol on a SPEC.md or design document: five fresh-context stages that test whether a stranger could understand and re-implement it.
commands.name: rnov-goldfish
commands.output: Consolidated findings in REVIEW.md with suite severities; per-stage reports in the run folder.
steps: Follow the `review` skill, Goldfish protocol section: semantic split first (Detailed Implementation header).
Stage 1 initial zoom-out, then stage 2 comprehension, stage 3 critic (lenses in parallel, synthesised), stage 4 intermediate zoom-out with the stage 1 report, stage 5 implementation readiness.
Each stage is a fresh reviewer; at most one re-audit per stage.
Consolidate into REVIEW.md with a traceability line per finding; per-stage reports live in the run folder.

commands.description: Run only the Goldfish comprehension stage on a document: can a fresh reader restate the feature and re-implement it from the document alone?
commands.name: rnov-goldfish-comprehension
commands.output: Restatement plus the list of guess points, each naming its section.
steps: Follow the `review` skill, Goldfish protocol, stage 2 (Comprehension).
Read only the target file, the files it references, and an optional baseline reading list — never the conversation that produced the document.
Restate the feature in your own words, then list every place you had to guess, assume, or could not tell.
Undefined terms, unexplained acronyms, assumed prerequisites, and vague explanations are findings, not style notes.

commands.description: Run only the Goldfish critic stage on a document: architecture, scalability, cost, faulty assumptions, and unmitigated risks, with the lenses in parallel.
commands.name: rnov-goldfish-critic
commands.output: Findings ordered by severity, each with evidence from the document.
steps: Follow the `review` skill, Goldfish protocol, stage 3 (Critic), over the feature range.
Run the lenses in parallel and synthesise them; do not let one lens's clean bill hide another's finding.
Cover architecture, scalability, cost and quota, faulty assumptions, unmitigated risks, heading structure and mandatory sections, fluff and jargon.

commands.description: Run only the Goldfish implementation-readiness stage: is there any design decision left to the implementer?
commands.name: rnov-goldfish-readiness
commands.output: Readiness verdict plus the list of decisions the document leaves open, if any.
steps: Follow the `review` skill, Goldfish protocol, stage 5 (Implementation readiness), over the detailed range.
Check the file list is complete with a rationale per file, test assertions are named, and no decision is left to the implementer.
Where code already exists, check the document against it for missing logic, unstated assumptions, and undocumented edge cases.

commands.argument-hint: [the hypothesis in two or three sentences]
commands.description: Run a six-lens parallel swarm on an anchored hypothesis: Contrarian, Cost, UX, Migration, Observability, Tech debt — fresh workers only.
commands.name: rnov-lens-swarm
commands.output: Deduplicated findings grouped by severity; unresolved items resolved, recorded as ADRs, or parked with owner and trigger.
steps: Follow the `grill` skill, Lens swarm section. Do not spawn the swarm until the readiness gate passes: the hypothesis is anchored in two or three sentences the human recognises, and the human confirms readiness.
Spawn six fresh workers, one per lens; each receives only the hypothesis and the artifacts it needs — no conversation history, no author claims.
Synthesise before reporting: dedup, group by severity (see `orchestrate`). A list of raw, overlapping findings is not a result.
At most two rounds per hypothesis; findings resolve into the decision tree, ADRs, or parked with an owner and a trigger.

commands.description: Document the team's own undocumented codebase bottom-up into per-directory README contracts, leaf first.
commands.name: rnov-bootstrap
commands.output: Per-directory README contracts with sentinel markers; placeholders logged as documentation owed, not as completed contracts.
commands.section: ## Bootstrap mode (own codebase, no design docs)
steps: Follow the `recon` skill, Bootstrap mode section. Discover breadth-first and prune test-only and empty directories; above fifteen directories, pause for human approval before any swarm is spawned.
Scout each directory read-only with bounded reads; write leaf Component Package contracts first, then parent Blueprints post-order.
Preserve human notes inside the sentinel markers; never overwrite an existing README wholesale.
Final pass: every section present and populated, every relative link resolves, verification targets match the test configuration.

commands.description: Sweep a tree's SPEC.md, DESIGN.md, and README contracts against the current code and report only the divergences.
commands.name: rnov-drift
commands.output: Differences-only report at docs/drift/<YYYY-MM-DD>-DRIFT_REPORT.md with coverage stated.
steps: Follow the `verify` skill, Drift sweep section. For each document, read it, locate the source it names, and compare against the current code.
Check the ADRs before flagging: intentional divergence is recorded with its ADR cited, not flagged as drift.
Every item carries its evidence (doc section and code location) and a severity from the suite's scale; triage findings like review findings (CONTEST with evidence, or PROPOSE FIX).
State the coverage plainly: the sweep is a read-and-judge comparison, bounded by what was actually read.

commands.anchor: Findings are classified as contract misread
commands.description: Run a blind-doubt pass on a risky, hard-to-reverse decision: the reviewer gets the artifact and the contract only, never the author's claims.
commands.name: rnov-blind-doubt
commands.output: Classified findings with the author's answer per class.
commands.section: ## Blind doubt review for risky decisions
steps: Follow the `review` skill, Blind doubt review section. The reviewer receives the artifact and the contract only — never the author's claim, reasoning, or confidence.
Classify findings as contract misread, valid and actionable, trade-off, or noise; the author answers each class differently.
One round by default; escalate to a stronger or cross-family reviewer by stakes, not ritually.
